player_action: I grab the bandit and start a grapple.
game_state: Fighter without Improved Grapple adjacent to a Medium bandit.
correct_ruling: Starting a grapple provokes an attack of opportunity from the target; if that AoO deals damage the grapple attempt fails. Then a melee touch attack to grab, followed by an opposed grapple check (BAB + Str mod + size modifier).
common_wrong_rulings: Grapple is an Athletics check vs Athletics/Acrobatics (5e).
Grappling does not provoke.

player_action: What's my grapple modifier? I'm a Small halfling rogue, BAB +3, Str 12.
correct_ruling: Grapple check = BAB + Str modifier + special size modifier; Small is -4. So +3 +1 -4 = +0.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > Grapple Checks (special size modifier)
common_wrong_rulings: Small creatures get +1 like on attack rolls.
Dex is used instead of Str.

player_action: I'm grappled. I want to cast fireball at the guy holding me.
game_state: Wizard grappled by an ogre; fireball has a somatic component.
correct_ruling: While grappling you can cast only spells with a casting time of 1 standard action or less, no somatic component, and whose material components you have in hand; fireball has a somatic component (and material), so it can't be cast. Even an eligible spell requires a Concentration check (DC 20 + spell level).
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling > Cast a Spell
common_wrong_rulings: You can cast normally with a Concentration check.
Grappled only reduces speed to 0 (5e).

player_action: I'm grappling the orc. I want to attack it with my longsword.
game_state: Fighter grappling an orc, holding a longsword.
correct_ruling: While grappling you can attack only with an unarmed strike, natural weapon, or a light weapon; a longsword (one-handed, not light) can't be used. You take a -4 penalty on such attacks.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling > Attack Your Opponent
common_wrong_rulings: Any weapon can be used with disadvantage.
No penalty.

player_action: My buddy is grappling the troll. I shoot my crossbow at the troll.
game_state: Ranger 30 ft away; ally and troll in a grapple.
correct_ruling: You may target the troll; it is engaged in melee with your ally so the normal -4 penalty for shooting into melee applies unless you have Precise Shot. (In 3.0 a grappler target was determined randomly; 3.5 dropped that.)
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > Attacking a grappler (if you're not grappling)
common_wrong_rulings: Determine randomly which grappler is hit (3.0 rule).
No penalty at all.
confidence_note: Unsure whether 3.5 SRD retains any random-target rule for attacks against grapplers; ruling assumes it does not.

player_action: I'm grappled by the ogre. Does it still get its Dex bonus to AC against my rogue friend's sneak attack?
game_state: Ogre grappling the fighter; rogue attacks the ogre from outside the grapple.
correct_ruling: Grappling creatures don't threaten any squares and lose their Dexterity bonus to AC against opponents they aren't grappling, so the rogue can sneak attack the ogre.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling (no threatened squares, lose Dex bonus vs. opponents you aren't grappling)
common_wrong_rulings: Grappling has no effect on AC.

player_action: I grappled the goblin last round. Now I want to pin it.
correct_ruling: To pin, win an opposed grapple check as an attack; the opponent is held immobile (but not helpless) for 1 round. A pinned creature loses its Dex bonus to AC and others get +4 on attacks against it (not the pinner).
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling > Pin Your Opponent
common_wrong_rulings: Pinned is the same as helpless, allowing coup de grace.
Pin lasts until escaped.

player_action: I want to escape the grapple by tumbling out.
game_state: Rogue grappled by a hobgoblin; rogue has Escape Artist ranks.
correct_ruling: You can escape with an opposed grapple check or an Escape Artist check opposed by the opponent's grapple check, as a standard action. Tumble isn't a grapple escape option.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling > Escape from Grapple
common_wrong_rulings: Use Acrobatics vs Athletics (5e).
Tumble DC 15 escapes.

player_action: I'm a Medium fighter. Can I grapple the Huge dragon?
correct_ruling: Core 3.5 grapple rules set no size limit on who you can grapple; instead each side adds its special size modifier to grapple checks (Medium +0, Huge +8), so the attempt is legal but very hard. Size limits apply to monster abilities such as improved grab, not to ordinary grapples.
common_wrong_rulings: You can't grapple a creature two sizes larger.
Size doesn't matter in a grapple.
confidence_note: Fairly confident 3.5 SRD has no size cap on starting a grapple (unlike improved grab); not checked line-by-line.

player_action: The monster with improved grab hits me with its bite. Does it provoke an AoO from me when it grapples?
game_state: Fighter hit by a creature with improved grab.
correct_ruling: Improved grab lets the creature start a grapple as a free action without provoking an attack of opportunity, and it doesn't need the initial touch attack.
common_wrong_rulings: It provokes like a normal grapple.

player_action: I'm grappling the cultist. I move him 10 feet to push him off the ledge.
game_state: Fighter grappling a cultist, both Medium.
correct_ruling: You can move while grappling by winning an opposed grapple check (standard action) to move up to half your speed, bringing the grappled creatures with you; you'd need to be able to move to the ledge; moving him into a square off the edge isn't a defined grapple option — it's a DM adjudication (bull rush is the usual way).
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling > Move
common_wrong_rulings: You can drag at full speed.
You can just throw him.

player_action: I have Improved Grapple, so I can't be grappled and everything I grab is automatically pinned.
correct_ruling: Improved Grapple only means you don't provoke an attack of opportunity when starting a grapple and gives +4 on grapple checks. It doesn't auto-pin or make you immune to grapples.
common_wrong_rulings: Improved Grapple grants advantage or auto-success.

player_action: I'm grappled. Do I still threaten squares and get my AoO against the goblin running past?
game_state: Fighter grappling an orc; a goblin runs past.
correct_ruling: No. While grappling you don't threaten any squares, so you get no attacks of opportunity.
common_wrong_rulings: Yes, grappling doesn't affect threatened squares.

player_action: I'm grappling and I want to deal damage to the orc with my bare hands.
game_state: Fighter (no Improved Unarmed Strike) grappling an orc.
correct_ruling: Win an opposed grapple check to deal unarmed strike damage (1d3 for Medium + Str); it is nonlethal unless you take -4 on the grapple check to make it lethal.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple > If You're Grappling > Damage Your Opponent
common_wrong_rulings: Normal lethal damage with no penalty.

player_action: I want to grab the ooze to hold it still. Does that even work on an amorphous blob?
correct_ruling: The SRD grapple rules don't generally exclude oozes; monster entries (e.g. engulf) specify interactions. Unless the creature entry grants immunity, it can be grappled, but the DM adjudicates odd anatomy and touching it may apply its acid/paralysis per its entry.
srd_reference: CombatII.rtf > Grapple; Monster entry: Gelatinous Cube
common_wrong_rulings: Oozes can never be grappled.
Grappling has no added risk.
confidence_note: Monster-specific grapple immunities vary; treat as DM-adjudicated.

player_action: I'm grappling one orc; a second orc wants to join the grapple to help.
correct_ruling: Others can join a grapple; up to four Medium (or eight Small... per size rules) can grapple one target. A joining creature makes the grapple check normally; when multiple grapplers, assistance via aid another may apply. The joining creature doesn't provoke from the grappled target if... normally joining requires the usual grab (provoking AoOs from threatening non-grappled foes).
common_wrong_rulings: Only one creature can grapple a target.
confidence_note: Exact joining procedure and numeric limits not verified against SRD text.
